claims.claim: typical surface seawater holds on the order of a million bacterial cells and ten million virus-like particles per millilitre
claims.definition: direct microscopic counts of marine systems; abundances vary with location, depth and season, but the orders of magnitude are robust
claims.measured_value: ~10^6 bacteria/ml; ~10^7 viruses/ml (varies by orders less between sites)
claims.authoritative_source: Whitman, Coleman & Wiebe 1998 (PNAS), 'Prokaryotes: the unseen majority'; marine viral ecology reviews (Suttle 2007)

claims.claim: a standard drop of water is about 0.05 millilitres, so one drop of surface seawater carries tens of thousands of bacteria and hundreds of thousands of viruses
claims.definition: approximately 20 metric drops per millilitre; multiply typical per-ml abundances by drop volume
claims.measured_value: drop ~0.05 ml; ~5x10^4 bacteria and ~5x10^5 virus particles per drop (order of magnitude)
claims.authoritative_source: pharmacopoeia drop-volume standard (~0.05 ml) combined with Whitman et al. 1998 abundances

claims.claim: average ocean salinity is about 3.5%, dominated by sodium and chloride ions
claims.definition: 35 grams of dissolved salts per kilogram of seawater on average; chloride and sodium are the largest contributors
claims.authoritative_source: NOAA ocean salinity facts; UNESCO/TEOS-10 seawater references

claims.claim: marine viruses infect bacteria and other microbes constantly; viral lysis redirects a substantial share of microbial biomass back into dissolved organic matter (the viral shunt) — commonly estimated at roughly a fifth to a quarter of bacterial production daily
claims.definition: the viral shunt converts particulate microbial biomass into dissolved organic carbon available to other microbes; daily lysed fraction estimates vary by study and system
claims.measured_value: ~20-25% of bacterial production lysed daily (studies span roughly 10-40%)
claims.authoritative_source: Suttle 2007 (Nature Reviews Microbiology), marine viruses; 'viral shunt' literature (Wilhelm & Suttle 1999)

claims.claim: diatoms, single-celled algae with glass shells, are responsible for roughly one-fifth of global photosynthetic production
claims.definition: diatom contribution to marine and global primary production estimated around 20% in synthesis literature; values vary by method
claims.authoritative_source: Falkowski et al. 2004 (Science) on ocean primary production; diatom ecology reviews (Armbrust 2009)

claims.claim: the drop's inhabitants span orders of scale: diatoms tens to hundreds of micrometres, bacteria around one micrometre, viruses tens to hundreds of nanometres, salt ions and dissolved molecules at sub-nanometre scale
claims.definition: size ranges from marine microbiology: bacteria ~0.5-2 um; viruses ~0.02-0.3 um; diatoms ~10-200 um; hydrated ions ~0.0002 um
claims.measured_value: log-scale spread of roughly one million-fold from ion to diatom
claims.authoritative_source: standard marine microbiology size references (Suttle 2007; general microbiology texts)
